# Keep native storage paths and application identity consistent

## Platform difference

Native code expecting desktop HOME or a hard-coded bundle-derived path may not use the writable storage intended for the OH app.

## Implementation

NipaPlay moves Rust torrent persistence away from HOME to an app-writable download-relative location. LocalSend repairs a Downloads path still containing the prior application identity and updates its distribution URL. InkNote supplies an application-support path to Rust and deliberately retains internal identifiers for continuity. Draftmark likewise initializes its Rust store below application-support storage; LocalSend's custom directory browser stays within its chosen app base.

## Applicability

Choose paths from the app context/platform path provider and pass them into native cores. Treat identifier changes as possible data/update continuity changes, not just branding.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

A directory browser rooted in app Downloads is not a general system-folder picker. App-private output does not guarantee user-visible export. Retained identifiers are a project decision; do not copy another project's bundle name or signing configuration.

## Verification

Test writable initialization, restart, upgrade/identity transitions, path containment and native-core access; verify user export separately from private storage.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
